statement: Let Z and S be affine schemes, with Z reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and S integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let g:Z→S be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let η be a generic point of S. Assume its fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. There exist an affine integral S′, a universal homeomorphism q:S′→S [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism], and a point η′ with q(η′)=η. Put Y=(Z×_S S′)_red, using the canonical nilradical reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-pc-fibre-product], and let p:Yη′→Spec κ(η′) be its fibre map. There exist a field F in the same universe as the schemes, a κ(η′)-algebra structure on F, and a quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dominant morphism h:Spec F→Yη′ such that F is separably generated over κ(η′) [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] and h followed by p equals Spec of the field algebra map. Scheme-theoretic dominance means injectivity of the map on the structure sheaves. No geometric reducedness or genericity of η′ is asserted.

proof.text: Write S=Spec A and Z=Spec B. The generic fibre ring B_K is the localization over the fraction field K of A, so is reduced; geometric irreducibility makes it a nonzero domain. Its fraction field L is finitely generated over K by finite presentation.

Apply the finite purely inseparable separably-generated field square, then replace the upper field by the compositum as in Tag 030R. A finitely generated separable subextension is separably generated. The reduced tensor F=(L tensor_K K′)_red is this field. Choose finite generators b_i of K′/K and multiply each by a nonzero denominator d_i so that its prime-power equation has coefficient in A. Let A′ be the actual A-subalgebra of K′ generated by these scaled elements. It is a finite domain with fraction field K′. Its integral radicial spectrum map q is surjective by lying over, and hence a universal homeomorphism. Lift η uniquely to η′; its residue field is K′.

Reduction commutes with localization, so Yη′ has coordinate ring (B tensor_A K′)_red. Tensoring B_K→L with K′ preserves injectivity by flatness of the field extension. Reducing an injection preserves injectivity because nilpotence is detected by an injective map. The resulting coordinate ring injection into F yields h:Spec F→Yη′ with zero kernel ideal sheaf. Both schemes are affine, making h quasi-compact. The field algebra compatibility gives h followed by p equal to Spec of the algebra map. In characteristic zero take K′=K. The nonempty generic fibre ensures all fraction fields are of nonzero domains.

proof_origin.note: Follows the affine radicial construction in the source, spelling out generator scaling, reduced tensor injection and the corresponding scheme-theoretically dominant morphism.

theorem exists_radicial_separating_generic_field
    {Z S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Z] [IsReduced Z] [IsAffine S] [IsIntegral S]
    (g : Z ⟶ S) [Flat g] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g]
    (η : S) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible (g.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (q : S' ⟶ S),
      IsAffine S' ∧ IsIntegral S' ∧ IsUniversalHomeomorphism q ∧
      ∃ η' : S', q η' = η ∧
        ∃ (F : Type u) (hF : Field F) (aF : Algebra (S'.residueField η') F),
          letI := hF
          letI := aF
          ∃ h : Spec (.of F) ⟶
              ((pullback g q).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd g q).fiber η',
            IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant h ∧ QuasiCompact h ∧
            Algebra.IsSeparablyGenerated (S'.residueField η') F ∧
            h ≫ ((pullback g q).nilradical.subschemeι ≫
              pullback.snd g q).fiberToSpecResidueField η' =
                Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S'.residueField η') F))
